how.intro: The colour comes from fixed rules in code, not from the AI. The AI only reads your question and explains the result.
how.rule_worst: We check every hour of your trip. The worst hour decides the colour.
how.rule_margin: Our own rule: a value within {pct}% of a caution line counts as caution. This rule is ours, not from a published source.
how.rule_missing: Our own rule: if any data is missing, or older than {hours} hours, we say caution. We never say safe without data.
how.rule_thunder: Our own rule: a forecast thunderstorm gives caution, not unsafe, because thunderstorm forecasts are uncertain.
how.rule_display: Wave period and direction are shown but do not change the colour, because no published source gives a limit.

faq.verdicts: SAFE means every hour of your trip is under all the caution lines. CAUTION means something is over a caution line, close to one, or has no data, so be careful. UNSAFE means the waves, wind or gusts reach the unsafe line: don't take a small boat out.
faq.how_decided: For every hour of your trip, at the sea point nearest your harbour, I check the waves, wind, gusts, thunderstorms and visibility. It's a caution from waves of {wave_c} metres, wind of {wind_c} or gusts of {gust_c} kilometres per hour, visibility of {vis_c} metres or less, or any thunderstorm. It's unsafe from waves of {wave_u} metres, wind of {wind_u} or gusts of {gust_u} kilometres per hour. The worst hour decides.
faq.sources: Each line comes from a published source: the World Meteorological Organization's marine manuals, the FAO's safety rules for small fishing boats, and the India Meteorological Department's fishermen warnings. Tap '{how}' to see each one.
faq.near_line: If a value is within {pct} percent of a caution line, I say caution rather than safe, because a forecast can be a little off. That rule is ours, not from a source.
faq.boats: These lines are for small open boats under 10 metres. A bigger boat can handle more, but I don't check for bigger boats.
faq.accuracy: A forecast is a best estimate, not a guarantee, and it gets less certain further ahead. I only look {window} hours ahead, and if the data is more than {stale} hours old I say caution. Always check the official warnings too.
faq.data_source: The weather data comes from Open-Meteo: waves from the {marine} model and wind from the {weather} model. Live data is refreshed every {cache} minutes.
faq.missing_data: If any hour of your trip has no data, I say caution, never safe.
faq.memory: This phone remembers only your usual harbour and trip length. The server keeps no conversations, and nothing else is stored.
faq.limits: I check sea safety for small boats from these harbours for the next {window} hours: waves, wind, gusts, thunderstorms and visibility, plus rain, temperature, sunrise and sunset. I can't check tides, currents or where the fish are.
